column2: The Pitfalls of KV Cache Compression
column8: effectively causing them to be completely ignored by the LLM
column9: Under benign multi-instruction prompts (IFEval; StreamingLLM, SnapKV, TOVA, H2O, K-Norm on Llama3.1 8B, Qwen2.5 14B), compression degrades some instructions much faster than others; system prompt leakage is a case study; compression method, instruction order and eviction bias drive it; simple eviction-policy fixes help.
column10: No active adversary crafting inputs to target eviction (leakage arises from benign compression, though leakage is a security outcome). Measures accuracy/leakage only, not memory or resource impact. Single-request, no multi-tenant serving.
column11: robustness: instruction loss and system-prompt leakage under eviction

column2: When Efficiency Meets Safety: A Benchmark Security Analysis of KV Cache Compression in Large Language Models
column8: where aggressive merging in shallow layers triggers functional head collapse, amplifying attack success rates
column9: Systematic jailbreak study across four model families: compression gives accidental robustness to optimization- and encoding-based attacks but merging-based compression amplifies human-designed jailbreak ASR; proposes Safe-CAM per-head merging restoring 0% ASR.
column10: Adversary is a jailbreaker seeking harmful output, not one targeting memory or compression ratio. No memory/resource attack measured. No multi-tenant serving setting.
column11: robustness: jailbreaks under compression; safety-aware merging

column2: AnchorKV: Safety-Aware KV Cache Compression via Soft Penalty with a Refusal Anchor
column8: fail to defend against jailbreak attacks
column9: Claims existing compression either fails to defend against jailbreaks or degrades safety alignment under aggressive eviction; proposes drop-in retention-score penalty along harmful key-space directions (refusal anchor).
column10: Adversary is a jailbreaker, not a resource attacker; does not test attacks adapted to AnchorKV's anchor beyond what abstract states. Accuracy/safety only, no memory exhaustion. No multi-tenant serving.

column2: RobustKV: Defending Large Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks via KV Eviction
column8: selectively removing critical tokens of harmful queries from key-value (KV) caches
column9: Uses eviction as a defense: jailbreak prompts inflate attention on their own tokens, so evicting low-importance tokens strips the hidden harmful query; claims an effectiveness-evasiveness dilemma against adaptive attackers.
column10: Studies an adversary (jailbreaker, including adaptive) but eviction is the defense, not the target. No memory/resource measurement. No multi-tenant serving. Shows attackers can shape attention importance, which is the lever for eviction-targeting attacks.
column11: adversary vs eviction scoring; eviction as defense

column2: Taming the Fragility of KV Cache Eviction in LLM Inference (DefensiveKV)
column8: we argue that this underlying assumption is inherently fragile
column9: Mean-aggregated importance scoring relies on a stability assumption that fails in extreme cases; defensive (worst-case-bounding) aggregation in linear time, plus layer-wise budgets, cuts quality loss 2.3x/4.3x at 20% cache over strongest baseline on 18 datasets.
column10: Worst-case is over benign data, not an adversary crafting inputs. Measures generation quality at fixed budget, not memory under attack. No multi-tenant serving.

column2: CriticalKV: Optimizing KV Cache Eviction from an Output Perturbation Perspective
column8: optimizes the worst-case output perturbation to identify critical entries
column9: Attention weights alone are insufficient for eviction; bounding worst-case output perturbation (using value states) roughly halves compression loss as a plug-in to existing eviction methods.
column10: Worst-case is analytic over outputs, not adversarial inputs. Accuracy only, no memory/resource attack. No multi-tenant serving.

column2: Semantic Integrity Matters: Benchmarking and Preserving High-Density Reasoning in KV Cache Compression (KVFundaBench, ShotKV)
column8: reasoning tasks exhibit severe Task-Dependent Degradation under aggressive compression due to disrupted CoT links
column9: Retrieval survives compression while reasoning degrades sharply; proposes ShotKV treating few-shot examples as units. This is the arXiv entry for the work the brief calls "Can LLMs maintain fundamental abilities under KV cache compression" (old title not shown on page, so not confirmed).
column10: Benign benchmarks only, no adversary. Accuracy and latency only, no memory exhaustion. No multi-tenant serving.

column2: Rethinking Key-Value Cache Compression Techniques for Large Language Model Serving
column8: compressing KV cache may lead to longer outputs, resulting in increased end-to-end latency
column9: Serving-side evaluation of compression: compressed models can emit longer outputs, erasing throughput/latency gains; compression benefits are workload-dependent. Closest evidence that compression savings can be negated (benignly).
column10: No adversary; the longer-output effect is not induced deliberately. Does measure serving resource/latency effects. No multi-tenant adversarial setting.
column11: resource: compression savings negated in serving

column2: Rethinking Latency Denial-of-Service: Attacking the LLM Serving Framework, Not the Model
column8: Fill first exhausts the global KV cache to induce Head-of-Line blocking
column9: Adversarial prompts fill KV cache memory and trigger repeated preemption in the scheduler, a serving-level DoS (Fill and Squeeze), using latency probing to estimate free cache.
column10: Adversary and resource impact both present, and it is a shared serving setting, but it does not involve KV compression or eviction policies at all; does not show forcing dense retention under a compressor.

column2: Can Transformer Memory Be Corrupted? Investigating Cache-Side Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
column8: systematically perturbs cached key vectors at selected layers and timesteps
column9: Treats the KV cache as an attack surface: perturbing cached keys propagates silently to outputs.
column10: Threat model assumes direct write access to cache, not input-only adversary manipulating compression. Output corruption, not memory/resource. No multi-tenant compression path.

column2: LLM Jailbreaks Exploit Attention Sinks
column8: We find that tokens in adversarial suffixes are prone to inducing attention sinks
column9: Adversarial suffixes create attention sinks; amplifying them raises jailbreak success. Shows adversarial text can control where attention mass goes, the signal eviction policies score on.
column10: Adversary present but goal is jailbreak, not eviction or memory; no compression evaluated. No resource or multi-tenant aspect.

column2: Interpreting the Repeated Token Phenomenon in Large Language Models
column8: the initial token receives disproportionately high attention scores
column9: Links repeated-token divergence to attention-sink mechanics; inputs can perturb sink behavior that StreamingLLM-style compressors rely on.
column10: Does not evaluate KV compression or eviction; no memory measurement; no serving. Search snippets mention a "cluster attack" but the abstract I saw did not, so not claimed.

column2: Robust KV Cache Management for LLM Serving under Output Token Length Uncertainty
column8: We present a robust KV cache management framework for LLM serving
column9: Distributionally robust (Wasserstein DRO) KV memory management under output-length uncertainty and workload shift in serving.
column10: Statistical robustness, no malicious users. Measures memory/serving outcomes. Multi-request serving but not adversarial multi-tenant; not about compression.
column11: hardening: DRO KV memory under shift

column2: A Probabilistic Interpretation of KV Cache Eviction
column8: correcting for evicted entries during decoding---a previously ignored problem---becomes feasible
column9: Recasts eviction probabilistically so the effect of evicted entries can be corrected at decode time; claims more robust than top-k heuristics.
column10: No adversary; benign tasks. Accuracy, not memory under attack. No multi-tenant.

column2: VeriCache: Turning Lossy KV Cache into Lossless LLM Inference
column8: almost all of these methods are inherently lossy
column9: Proposes making lossy KV compression lossless (verification-style), giving an output guarantee regardless of input. Strongest "guarantee" direction found.
column10: No adversary studied; an adversary could still raise verification failure rate and cost (not measured). Resource cost of fallback under adversarial input unmeasured. No multi-tenant.

column2: H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models
column8: a small portion of tokens contributes most of the value when computing attention scores
column9: Canonical accumulated-attention token eviction (heavy hitters).
column10: No adversary; benign benchmarks. Memory savings shown, but assumes sparse attention that an input could defeat. No multi-tenant.

column2: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks (StreamingLLM)
column8: the emergence of attention sink is due to the strong attention scores towards initial tokens
column9: Keep initial sink tokens plus a recent window for bounded-memory streaming.
column10: No adversary; memory bounded by design (fixed window), so it cannot be forced to max occupancy but can be forced to drop content. No multi-tenant.

column2: SnapKV: LLM Knows What You are Looking for Before Generation
column8: this robust pattern can be obtained from an 'observation' window located at the end of the prompts
column9: Prompt-end observation window selects which prefill KV to keep. Relies on query at prompt end, which a user controls.
column10: No adversary; "robust" means across benign data. Memory/speed measured benignly. No multi-tenant.

column2: PyramidKV: Dynamic KV Cache Compression based on Pyramidal Information Funneling
column8: allocating more cache in lower layers and less in higher ones
column9: Layer-wise budget allocation based on attention funneling.
column10: No adversary; benign. Fixed budgets, accuracy-focused. No multi-tenant.

column2: Ada-KV: Optimizing KV Cache Eviction by Adaptive Budget Allocation for Efficient LLM Inference
column8: Base on this, we propose Ada-KV, the first head-wise adaptive budget allocation strategy.
column9: Head-wise adaptive budget allocation for eviction.
column10: No adversary. Total budget fixed, so adversary cannot inflate memory but can steer allocation (untested). No multi-tenant.

column2: Transformers are Multi-State RNNs (TOVA)
column8: We introduce a novel, training-free compression policy
column9: TOVA: evict token with lowest current attention, a fixed-size multi-state view.
column10: No adversary; benign. No resource-attack measurement. No multi-tenant.

column2: Scissorhands: Exploiting the Persistence of Importance Hypothesis for LLM KV Cache Compression at Test Time
column8: only pivotal tokens, which had a substantial influence at one step
column9: Persistence-of-importance hypothesis justifying eviction; the assumption DefensiveKV (B5) calls fragile.
column10: No adversary; hypothesis tested on benign data. No multi-tenant.

column2: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache
column8: the key cache should be quantized per-channel
column9: 2-bit asymmetric KV quantization (per-channel keys, per-token values).
column10: No adversary; outlier-channel assumptions could be attacked by crafted activations (untested). Memory saving fixed ratio, cannot be defeated by input. No multi-tenant.

column2: KVQuant: Towards 10 Million Context Length LLM Inference with KV Cache Quantization
column8: Our method enables serving LLaMA-7B with a context length of up to 1 million on a single A100-80GB GPU
column9: Low-bit KV quantization with outlier handling enabling very long contexts.
column10: No adversary; dense-and-sparse outlier storage could grow with adversarial outliers (untested). No multi-tenant.

column2: Palu: Compressing KV-Cache with Low-Rank Projection
column8: a KV-Cache compression framework that utilizes low-rank projection to reduce inference-time LLM memory usage.
column9: Low-rank projection compression of KV.
column10: No adversary; OOD inputs off the calibration subspace untested. No multi-tenant.

column2: Inference-Time Hyper-Scaling with KV Cache Compression (DMS)
column8: DMS delays token eviction, implicitly merging representations and preserving critical information.
column9: Learned eviction (Dynamic Memory Sparsification) trading cache memory for more reasoning tokens.
column10: No adversary; learned policy's OOD behavior untested. Memory measured benignly. No multi-tenant.

column2: KVzip: Query-Agnostic KV Cache Compression with Context Reconstruction
column8: a query-agnostic KV cache eviction method enabling effective reuse of compressed KV caches
column9: Query-agnostic compression whose compressed cache is reused across queries, i.e. compression baked into a shared/reused prefix.
column10: No adversary. Reuse of a compressed context across queries (and possibly users) creates a place where one input's compression decisions affect others; not studied. No multi-tenant security analysis.

column2: NVIDIA kvpress (GitHub repo)
column8: LLM KV cache compression made easy.
column9: NVIDIA library of KV compression presses for Hugging Face transformers pipelines; de facto benchmarking harness.
column10: No security/adversarial content; README integrates with HF transformers, not vLLM or a production engine. No multi-tenant.

column2: Expected Attention: KV Cache Compression by Estimating Attention from Future Queries Distribution
column8: a comprehensive library to enable researchers to implement and benchmark KV cache compression methods
column9: Closed-form expected-attention scoring from activation statistics; releases KVPress. Scoring assumes a distribution of future queries.
column10: No adversary; distributional assumption on queries is exactly what OOD/adversarial queries violate (untested). No multi-tenant.

column2: KVzap: Fast, Adaptive, and Faithful KV Cache Pruning
column8: they have not yet been adopted in major inference engines due to speed--accuracy trade-offs
column9: Fast adaptive pruning aimed at engine adoption; states pruning methods are not yet adopted in major inference engines.
column10: No adversary. Adaptive (input-dependent) pruning ratio means input could choose low compression (untested). No multi-tenant.

column2: SCBench: A KV Cache-Centric Analysis of Long-Context Methods
column8: existing benchmarks often evaluate in single-request, neglecting the full lifecycle of the KV cache in real-world use
column9: Benchmark of compression/sparse methods under shared-context, multi-turn KV reuse.
column10: Benign benchmarks only, no adversary; accuracy focus; multi-request reuse but not multi-tenant isolation.

column2: KV Cache Compression, But What Must We Give in Return? A Comprehensive Benchmark of Long Context Capable Approaches
column8: no existing work has comprehensively benchmarked these methods in a reasonably aligned environment
column9: Aligned benchmark of compression families (quantization, eviction, etc.) on long-context tasks.
column10: Benign only; no adversary; no memory-attack; no multi-tenant.

column2: KVCache-Factory (GitHub repo)
column8: Unified KV Cache Compression Methods for Auto-Regressive Models
column9: Unified implementations (StreamingLLM, H2O, SnapKV, PyramidKV, AdaKV, HeadKV, KIVI, KVQuant, GEAR, etc.), usable as attack testbed.
column10: No adversarial or security content; research harness, not a serving engine; no multi-tenant.

column2: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?
column8: almost all models exhibit large performance drops as the context length increases
column9: Synthetic long-context benchmark widely used to score compression (e.g. KVzap on RULER).
column10: Not about compression itself; benign; no adversary, memory, or multi-tenant.
